questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Exploring Icelands' nature

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere with beautiful nature where I could go hiking, and a university with interesting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a few very nice and helpful introduction days where we got to know all of the exchange students, and got useful information about living and studying in Iceland.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy, I found accommodation on HousingAnywhere.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in downtown Reykjavik which was nice, but it does mean that the commute to the university was a bit longer (15 min walk + 5 min busride)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing is available both through the student housing or finding your own spot through HousingAnywhere or similar. Both are very expensive though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty straight forward. I had one course cancelled due to low registration which caused some difficulty with having to re-do my learning agreement etc. Other than that fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office at RU was were helpful - they helped me get my learning agreement signed etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had one class cancelled due to low registration, other than that I got all the courses i signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Wait with doing the learning agreement until you have your courses proved by RU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Maybe a bit lower level than the courses at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit different. The courses usually all have oral exam and your final grade consist of both participation, assignments/presentations throughout the semester and then the final exam. Requires a bit more effort throughout the semester, but the exam at the end is easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Entertainment law, Copyright and AI, International Law of the Sea, Private Equity Law and EU regulation of financial services.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Law of the Sea was super interesting and fun to have in Iceland where this subject is super relevant. We also had an excursion to the coast guard hangar with the course where we got to see their helicopters and airplane.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are a bit more expensive than in Denmark, but not much. Alcohol is SUPER expensive especially if your buying it at a bar etc. Same goes for eating at restaurants, also very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The tutors at RU and ESN Iceland were very good at hosting different social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the swimming pool culture in Iceland! So many good hotspring/hottubs - recommend Nautholsvik right by RU which has a very nice hottub  next to the beach.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car with your friends and drive around in the beautiful nature - go on some hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, quite similar culture to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the intro days before the actual semester starts - here I made a lot of friends with the other exchange students both those studying the same as me, and those from other faculties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Swimming pool culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend it to fellow outdoorsy people - Iceland is such a beautiful country. Don't come just because if Reykjavik, the city is very small, the great things lie beyond the city.

Have patience with the weather, the days in the winter are very short, and even in spring it can be super cold, snowy and very windy, but when the good days comes around it's absolutely amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reykjavik and Iceland in general is all about cars. There's very little public transport so getting around requires a car. For short term rentals I recommend Reykjavik Car Rentals, good pricing and super easy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends, and experiencing the amazing nature in Iceland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making it through the periods during winter with very little daylight and weather conditions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
